content:
Alice Chen: FYI — customer (org: papertrail-ai) opened a support ticket: their requests to /v1/generate are intermittently returning 403 'Invalid API key'. They see it from web app and backend clients. Root ts: 1932109876. Repro steps from customer included below.

Alice Chen: repro steps they gave: 1) POST /v1/generate with org API key 2) sometimes get 200, sometimes 403 with body: `{
  "error": "Invalid API key"
}` 3) header `x-request-id` changes each try.

Ben Kapoor: huh. do we have examples of entitlement checks masquerading as auth? I know we've had the caching-race bug before.

Alice Chen: they said this started after their seats were reduced from 12 -> 8 last week. billing portal shows downgrade succeeded.

Maria Ortiz: pinging from Billing — we did process the downgrade. The tenant had temporary overage, then we applied new sku on 2026-09-01T14:22Z. seat_count now 8. No pending invoices.

Jordan Park: can we get server logs for one of the failing request ids? ask customer for `x-request-id` header and a timestamp.

Alice Chen: provided `x-request-id: req_0a8f3c9f` at 2026-09-02T09:12:03Z. Attached raw response: status 403, body `{"error":"Invalid API key"}` and headers: `x-error-code: forbidden.plan`, `x-entitlement-check: failed`, `x-cache-hit: miss`.

Ben Kapoor: aha `x-error-code: forbidden.plan` — backend already sets a distinct header. but client surface shows generic "Invalid API key" string. That's our mapping layer masking the real cause.

Jordan Park: digging into logs for req_0a8f3c9f. server log snippet: 
```
[2026-09-02T09:12:03.123Z] auth: api_key=org_pk_live_xxx tenant=papertrail-ai req=req_0a8f3c9f
[2026-09-02T09:12:03.124Z] entitlement_check: feature=generate allowed=false reason=plan_limit product=llm-inference tier=standard
[2026-09-02T09:12:03.125Z] response: status=403 body={"code":"forbidden.plan","message":"entitlement check failed: seats_exceeded"}
```
Jordan Park: so entitlement check returned forbidden.plan and our response translator overwrote the body with auth fallback when `auth` and `billing` headers present. looks like older SDKs treat a 403 as invalid token.

SRE Oncall: also noting `x-cache-hit: miss` — I see a race where plan sync runs and the in-memory plan cache returns stale seats for a microsecond while billing sync updates. if a request hits in that window we deny. Redis TTL is 2s and replication lag in eu-west was ~500ms during window.

Ben Kapoor: possible two issues: (1) our error mapping layer masks entitlement reasons with generic auth message and (2) short-lived plan cache inconsistency causing flapping denies. both needed.

Alice Chen: customer impact: intermittent 403s visible in web UI, they think API key rotated or invalid — major confusion. They escalated to account team.

Maria Ortiz: what mitigation can we provide quickly? Can we surface a clearer error to them?

Jordan Park: immediate mitigation: change translator to preserve `x-error-code` and body when header `x-entitlement-check: failed` present. push a config change to prod routing layer (no runtime restart). That will show `{"code":"forbidden.plan","message":"seats_exceeded"}` to clients and reduce confusion. I can patch now.

Ben Kapoor: agree. also add a temporary soft fallback: if entitlement_check fails and feature is non-critical, allow request for 30s grace for tenants that just downgraded — but that's riskier. maybe only for generate and small token counts.

SRE Oncall: for the cache race: increase Redis replication check and extend TTL to 5s for plan cache for a hotfix window (30m), then revert after we stabilize. I'm going to open a runbook step and apply in eu-west first.

Alice Chen: customer-facing message draft: "We're seeing intermittent 403s due to plan/seat sync timing; your API key is valid. We're rolling a fix to surface a clearer error and applying a cache stabilization. No action required on your side. We'll follow up when fully resolved." ok to send?

Maria Ortiz: ok from billing. include note we already processed downgrade. include link to billing change in the message.

Ben Kapoor: engineering plan: 1) quick patch to response translator (preserve message + distinct code) — Jordan 15m 2) deploy translator patch to routing (canary 5% -> 100%) — Jordan 30m 3) extend plan cache TTL in eu-west -> 5s for 30m window — SRE Oncall 10m 4) create postmortem and propose longer-term fix: strong eventual consistency for plan state or use write-through cache on billing update.

Jordan Park: starting translator patch now. psuedo patch: 
```
if headers['x-entitlement-check']=='failed':
  http.response.body = original_body  # keep forbidden.plan
else:
  http.response.body = coerce_to_auth_message(response)
```
SRE Oncall: applying TTL change to redis key `tenant:plan:*` in eu-west cluster. will monitor.

Alice Chen: sent customer note with above wording. customer replied: "Thanks — can you confirm we won't be blocked during business hours?"

Ben Kapoor: if we keep TTL increase + translator patch we should drop client confusion to near zero. still want to avoid the soft-allow approach.

Maria Ortiz: opened billing ticket BLG-4532 to document the change and link to customer.

Jordan Park: translator patch deployed to canary at 2026-09-02T09:40Z. Observed sample of 50 requests -> 0 misclassified messages, 2 entitlement-denied responses (403 + forbidden.plan) as expected. Rolling to 100% now.

SRE Oncall: TTL increase applied. replication lag dropped to 120ms and no further fails in last 20m.

Alice Chen: customer confirmation: "we're no longer seeing Invalid API key — now we get seats_exceeded message. we'll review seats and adjust." they asked for guidance on how SDK surfaces this.

Ben Kapoor: follow-up: file SDK issue to map `forbidden.plan` -> explicit UI message like "Account seats exceeded: contact billing or upgrade". tagging eng-sdks.

Alice Chen: created support ticket update and scheduled a brief cross-team postmortem for tomorrow. thank you everyone :thumbsup:

Jordan Park: postmortem action items: - change error mapping to preserve entitlement error codes (done) - add metrics for `forbidden.plan` rate per region - implement write-through plan cache on billing updates - improve billing->control plane sync observability

SRE Oncall: I'll keep TTL at 5s for next 2 hours then revert. monitoring alert already set for `forbidden.plan` spike.

Alice Chen: closing the thread on our end. tagging INC-1234 and BLG-4532 for reference.
